tasks.title: Задача 1
tasks.statement:
Star rise in Moletai. An observer in Moletai recorded that a star culminated at 02:54 and set at 05:45 оп

September 8, 2013. Effects of irregularities of the horizon should not be taken into account.

1.1. At what time will the star rise on September 9, 2013?

1.2. In approximately which direction do you need to wait for the rising of the star? Choose one of the alternatives:
№, МЕ, Е, SE, $, SW, ХУ, NW. Draw a picture with an explanation.

parts.question: Приведите полное решение (с доказательством или выводом).
parts.reference:
1.1. The time elapsed from the rising of the star to culmination is equal to the time elapsed from
culmination to set. Therefore, on September 8, this star rose at 02:54 — 02:51 = 0:03. The next time the star
will rise after a sidereal day, equal to 23:56, that is, at 23:59 but still on September 8. On September 9 the
star will rise after one more sidereal day, that is at 23:55.

tasks.statement:

4.1. The outskirts of Dubingiai in the XVIII century were located on the same latitude as where they are
located іп the ХХІ century, that is, at about latitudes 54.7° — 55.29 (latitudes of Vilnius and Moletai
respectively, may be found from the map). The value of 23.5°, the inclination of the equatorial plane of the
ecliptic, also almost has not changed (strictly speaking, it had declined by about one arc minute). Thus, at
the middays of the winter solstice in the XVIII century in the outskirts of the town Dubingiai the sun was

hw = 90° — 55.0° — 23.5° = 11.5°,

at the middays of the summer solstice — at an altitude about
hg = 90° — 55.0° + 23.5° = 58.5°.

tasks.title: Задача 6
tasks.statement:
Supernova remnant. An X-ray image of supernova remnant (SNR) Cas A located at a distance of d = 3400 рс was
obtained using Chandra Space Observatory. The negative of this image is shown in Fig. SNR. The boundaries of
the SNR region are marked by a circle. The scale of the image is shown in the upper left corner of the figure. A dot
located close to the center of the circle is the neutron star — the remaining core of the collapsed star. The
rectangular marks outside the circle are given for the reference when determining the center of the circle.

Assume that the amount of energy released in the supernova explosion was about Egy = 1046 J, 1% of which drives
the expansion of the remnant. The average density of the matter in the SNR is р= 107 kg/m’,
6.1. Estimate the age of the SNR Cas A.
6.2. Calculate the average velocity of the motion of the neutron star from the center of the SNR.
